No board recommendation or advisor is named. No deal terms. Watch for potential OTC trading or alternative venue listing.

BYAH.company: Park Ha Biological Technology Co., Ltd.

GWH-WT.brief: ESS Tech disclosed it received a NYSE deficiency notice on June 9, 2026, for failing the $1.00 minimum bid-price rule under Section 802.01C, as its 30-day average closing price was $0.98. The company has six months to cure, potentially via a reverse stock split; no board recommendation or advisor was named. The notice is not an immediate delisting; trading continues. The cure requires closing at or above $1.00 for the last trading day of any month with a 30-day average that day at least $1.00. Shareholder approval may be needed. Watch for reverse-split plans or potential NYSE extension, with risk-arb focus on compliance timeline and equity overhang.

SAFX.brief: XCF Global, Inc. filed an S-4 registration statement with the SEC on June 12, 2026, relating to mergers involving XCF Global, DevvStream Corp., and Southern Energy Renewables Inc. The preliminary joint proxy statement/prospectus outlines a proposed transaction combining these entities. No specific terms (price per share, consideration, premium, or expected close date) were disclosed in the filing. The board of XCF Global has not yet issued a formal recommendation in the preliminary filing. Paul Hastings LLP and Shumaker, Loop & Kendrick, LLP serve as legal advisors. The registration statement must become effective before securities can be issued. The regulatory clock begins with SEC review of the S-4. What to watch: final deal terms, financing details, and stockholder votes.

BANR.brief: Banner Corporation filed an S-4/A registration statement for its acquisition of Pacific Financial Corporation via merger. Under the April 30, 2026 agreement, Pacific Financial shareholders will receive Banner common stock in a stock-for-stock transaction; exact exchange ratio and implied value are not specified in the filing. Each Pacific Financial share will be converted into Banner shares, and Bank of the Pacific will merge into Banner Bank post-close. The merger is subject to regulatory approvals, shareholder votes, and customary conditions. No board recommendation or advisor is named in this excerpt. The transaction is structured as a tax-free reorganization. Focus on shareholder vote timing and regulatory clearance for risk-arb spread.

EURKU.brief: Eureka Acquisition Corp, a Cayman Islands SPAC, filed an amended S-4 registration statement for its business combination with Marine Thinking Inc., a Canadian maritime tech company. Terms were not restated in this filing; the original deal structure is referenced but not detailed here. The board has not issued a new recommendation. The registration statement provides proxy/prospectus for shareholder vote. Structurally, the deal requires SEC effectiveness and shareholder approval. No break fee, premium, or other terms were disclosed. Watch for SEC review timeline and shareholder vote scheduling; the risk-arb spread depends on full terms from prior filings.

NVAAF.brief: Nova Minerals Ltd filed Form 15 to terminate its SEC reporting obligations after a redomiciliation to the U.S. Under a Scheme of Arrangement, Nova Minerals became a wholly-owned subsidiary of new Nevada parent Nova Minerals Corp. Holders received: one CDI per ASX ordinary share, one US Holdco common share per 12 OTC shares or per ADS, and three US Holdco warrants per Nova Minerals warrant. The board supported the scheme; no advisor named. The exchange listing moves from Nasdaq to NYSE American, effective June 17, 2026. Watch for smooth trading transition and potential arb on the exchange switch.

NIVFW.brief: NewGenIvf Group Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting entry into an additional share purchase agreement to acquire a further 4% equity interest in PredicXion Group Limited (K25.ai). Total consideration is US$4,000,000, comprising US$1,900,000 in cash or digital assets and 1,500,000 newly issued Class A ordinary shares. A US$100,000 cash deposit is due at signing, with the balance due by September 30, 2026. Upon completion, NewGenIvf will hold an aggregate 10% stake based on an implied valuation of US$100 million for PredicXion. The shares issued are restricted under Section 4(a)(2) and Regulation S. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions; no board recommendation or advisor is named. Watch for regulatory approvals and share delivery mechanics.

MXCT.brief: MaxCyte, Inc. disclosed in an 8-K filing that on June 10, 2026, it received a Nasdaq notice confirming the company regained compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement (Listing Rule 5450(a)(1)) for continued listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The staff determined that for the 10 consecutive business days ending June 9, 2026, the closing bid price was $1.00 or greater. The matter is now closed. No terms, percentages, or dates beyond compliance reinstatement were stated. No board or advisor action was noted. Watch for potential future price volatility or operational updates as the company remains listed.

BGMSP.brief: Bio Green Med Solution, Inc. filed an S-4 registration statement on June 16, 2026, in connection with a business combination. The filing does not disclose specific deal terms such as price per share, premium, or expected close date. No board recommendation or financial advisor is identified. The transaction involves the issuance of securities and is subject to SEC review and shareholder approval. The S-4 includes historical financials for the company and its subsidiary, Future NRG Sdn Bhd. Regulatory clearance under the HSR Act may apply. The risk-arb angle focuses on the completion timeline and potential shareholder vote.

DKS.brief: Dick's Sporting Goods files S-4/A registration statement for an exchange offer covering up to $381.9M of 4.000% Senior Notes due 2029. The issuer is exchanging outstanding notes issued September 11, 2025, for registered notes of like principal with substantially identical terms. The board has not been cited for a formal recommendation; Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz serves as legal counsel. Mechanics: no cash consideration, no premium; the exchange is intended to satisfy registration obligations under the Securities Act. The SEC registration statement remains subject to effectiveness. Risk-arb angle: no price arbitrage given the no-cash, same-terms structure; focus on SEC review timeline.

XTND.brief: Xtend AI Robotics, Inc. filed an amended S-4 registration statement for a business combination between its subsidiary, Xtend Reality Expansion Ltd. (Israeli), and JFB Construction Holdings (Nevada). JFB stockholders will vote by written consent. The deal consideration structure—cash, stock, or mix—is not specified in this filing. No board recommendation or advisor is disclosed. The registration is preliminary, subject to SEC effectiveness. Regulatory timing depends on SEC review and stockholder consent. Risk-arb focus: watch for definitive merger terms, shareholder support, and any regulatory hurdles under CFIUS given Xtend's Israeli domicile.

GENC.brief: Gencor Industries filed an 8-K disclosing it received a delinquency notice from NYSE American on May 19, 2026 for failing to timely file its Q1 2026 Form 10-Q. The company had a six-month cure period to regain compliance. On June 12, 2026, Gencor filed the delinquent 10-Q, and on June 15, 2026, NYSE confirmed the company had regained compliance with Section 1007 of the NYSE American Company Guide, removing it from the late filers list. No monetary terms, premiums, or board recommendations were involved. The event is a standard compliance cure with no risk-arb implications; the key watch item is any future filing delays that could re-trigger delisting risk.

GCGRU.company: General Catalyst Global Resilience Merger Corp.

GNL-PD.brief: Global Net Lease, Inc. filed Amendment No. 1 to its S-4 registration statement on June 17, 2026, in connection with its proposed merger with Modiv Industrial, Inc. The terms of the transaction are not specified in this filing; the proxy statement/prospectus remains preliminary and subject to completion. No board recommendation, advisor, price per share, premium, or closing timeline is disclosed. The filing registers securities to be issued in the merger and notes all conditions must be satisfied or waived before effectiveness. Risk-arb watchers should monitor subsequent amendments for definitive terms, including exchange ratio, valuation, and shareholder vote mechanics.

SEQC.brief: SeeQC, Inc. filed Amendment No. 1 to its Form S-4 on June 17, 2026, in connection with its business combination with Allegro Merger Corp. The merger agreement, entered January 16, 2026, provides that Allegro will merge into a SeeQC subsidiary, with Allegro security holders receiving up to 6,434,293 shares of SeeQC common stock. No per-share price, premium, or deal value is stated. The filing is preliminary; no board recommendation or financial advisor is cited. The transaction is structured as a stock-for-merger consideration. Risk-arb watchers should monitor SEC effectiveness and stockholder votes; the low premium and regulatory timeline are key watchpoints.

NHPAP.brief: National Healthcare Properties, Inc. issued an issuer tender offer to repurchase up to $100M aggregate of its 7.375% Series A and 7.125% Series B Cumulative Redeemable Perpetual Preferred Stock at $22.50 per share in cash. The offers expired June 16, 2026; preliminary results announced June 17, 2026. The board has not disclosed a recommendation or advisor in this filing. Mechanics include settlement by Computershare Inc. as depositary; final results pending confirmation. No premium stated relative to par or market. The risk-arb angle focuses on the final acceptance proration and any potential market reaction to the buyback completion.

LC.brief: LendingClub Corp voluntarily delisted its common stock from the NYSE, filing Form 25 under Rule 12d2-2(c) on June 18, 2026. The delisting, authorized by the issuer, became effective the same day. No consideration, premium, or board recommendation was disclosed. The removal cuts the exchange listing and Section 12(b) registration, reducing public market liquidity and regulatory disclosure obligations. With no buyout or third-party bid, risk arbitrage is absent; watch for subsequent deregistration under Section 12(g) or a potential going-private transaction.

HKD.brief: The Generation Essentials Group (TGE), a subsidiary of AMTD Digital Inc., filed a Form 6-K announcing a share repurchase program of up to US$10 million of its ordinary shares. TGE expects to fund repurchases from existing cash balance, with timing subject to Rule 10b-18/10b5-1. Concurrently, controlling shareholder AMTD Digital Inc., directors, and management voluntarily agreed to a two-year lock-up. The board believes shares are drastically undervalued given a 17.7% increase in total asset value to ~US$1.7 billion. No premium, price, or advisor named. What to watch: open-market execution risk and potential for increased buyback size.

AMTD.brief: AMTD IDEA Group filed a Form 6-K attaching an announcement by its subsidiary, The Generation Essentials Group (TGE), of a share repurchase program and a voluntary lock-up by its controlling shareholder. TGE's board authorized up to $10 million in open-market or private repurchases, to be funded from existing cash, aiming to enhance shareholder value given the stock's discount to net asset value. The controlling shareholder, AMTD Digital, along with directors and management, agreed to a two-year lock-up on TGE shares. The repurchases are subject to Rule 10b-18/10b5-1 compliance. Ordinary-course buyback with a controlling-shareholder lock-up; no tender offer premium or specific price terms. Watch for execution pace and asset value updates from recent hotel acquisitions.

AXIA-P.brief: AXIA Energia S.A., a Brazilian electric utility, filed a Form 6-K reporting a Board-approved partial mandatory redemption of 576,923 of its outstanding Class C preferred shares (PNC Shares), representing ~0.0951% of such shares, for an aggregate R$30,000,000.00 (implied price per share R$52.00). Holders may elect to convert redeemed PNC Shares into common shares at a 1.1:1 ratio (Partial Elective Conversion), though ADS holders are excluded from conversion. The redemption is pro rata, with fractional entitlements disregarded. Redemption occurs July 7, 2026; ADS payment follows later. This is a partial return of capital, not an issuer tender for all shares. Watch for treatment of fractional ADS positions.

BBAR.brief: Banco BBVA Argentina S.A. filed a Form 6-K announcing the second of three cash dividend installments, as resolved by the April 28, 2026 shareholders' meeting and authorized by the Argentine Central Bank on May 15, 2026. The dividend totals ARS 23,003,675,041, equating to ARS 37.5441433549 per share (representing a nominal 3,754% of capital stock). The record date is July 1, 2026, with payment starting July 6, 2026, through Caja de Valores S.A. ADS holders receive payment via Bank of New York Mellon on potentially differing dates. Withholdings apply for Personal Property Tax and a 7% income tax. This is a routine capital return, not a special situation, with no deal mechanics or risk-arb angle.

BCDRF.brief: Banco Santander filed a Form 6-K reporting ongoing share repurchases under a buyback program announced February 4, 2026. Between June 11-17, 2026, the bank repurchased 10,708,137 shares across XMAD and CEUX venues at weighted average prices ranging from €10.5131 to €11.7919. Cumulative purchases total €3,376,585,780, representing 67.1% of the maximum investment amount and 17.2% of outstanding shares. The buyback is executed under EU Market Abuse Regulation. The cash-based tender reduces equity overhang and signals management's view of undervaluation. Watch for program completion timelines and impact on EPS.

BRSL.brief: Brightstar Lottery PLC filed a Form 6-K announcing repurchases of 935,500 ordinary shares under its pre-existing $500 million buyback program. Shares were acquired in three tranches on May 22, May 29, and June 5, 2026, at prices ranging from $10.75 to $11.59 per share, for an aggregate cost of $10,483,880.54. The repurchased shares will be held in treasury. No board recommendation or advisor was named, as this is a routine open-market buyback execution. The filing relates to a foreign private issuer's capital return program; no shareholder vote or tender offer was involved. The buyback reduces outstanding share count and supports earnings per share. Watch for future repurchase activity and any program updates or suspensions.

CSCIF.brief: COSCIENS Biopharma Inc. filed a Form 6-K on June 18, 2026, reporting results of its annual general meeting and the appointment of Peter H. Puccetti as permanent full-time President and CEO, effective immediately. Puccetti, previously Chairman and Interim CEO since November, will continue to strengthen operational performance and align resources with strategic priorities. Shareholders approved the re-election of directors, re-appointment of Deloitte LLP as auditors, and a Share Capital Amendment involving a 1:150 consolidation followed immediately by a 50:1 split (net effect: 1:3 split). The board supported both actions. No deal terms apply; the structural change is share consolidation and split. Watch for further details on the capital amendment execution timeline; risk-arb angle minimal.

EMBJ.brief: Embraer S.A. filed a Form 6-K announcing its Board of Directors declared interest on equity (IoE) for Q2 2026, totaling R$ 200,000,000, equivalent to R$ 0.28096472120 per share. The IoE will be imputed to mandatory dividends for fiscal year 2026. Shareholders of record on B3 as of June 23, 2026, and NYSE ADS holders as of July 2, 2026, are eligible. Payment is scheduled for May 24, 2027, without adjustment or additional remuneration. The depositary bank is JPMorgan Chase. Watch for final per-share amounts after treasury share adjustments and any changes to the payment timeline.

STOHF.brief: Equinor ASA filed a Form 6-K reporting a share buy-back for its employee share programs. The buy-back program, announced 4 Feb 2026, runs 13 Feb 2026 to 15 Jan 2027, with a total purchase amount of NOK 1,971,000,000 and a maximum of 19,600,000 shares. On 15 Jun 2026, Equinor purchased 486,072 own shares at an average price of NOK 327.1115 per share. After the transaction, Equinor holds 66,774,249 own shares, or 2.61% of share capital. The shares are intended for employee incentive programs and capital reduction. This is a routine capital return filing with no special-situation premium or strategic change; watch for continued buy-back pace and share capital reduction progress.

ERIXF.brief: Ericsson filed a Form 6-K on June 18, 2026, announcing the appointment of David Hammarwall as new Head of Business Area Networks, effective October 1, 2026. He succeeds Per Narvinger, who becomes President and CEO of the company on the same date. The filing contains no financial terms, transaction details, board recommendations, or advisors—it is purely an executive personnel change. No shareholder vote or regulatory approvals are required. This is a routine management succession filing, not a special situation. Therefore, it does not fall under any merger or special-situations category beyond a standard management change announcement.

TGE-WT.brief: The Generation Essentials Group (TGE) filed a Form 6-K announcing a share repurchase program of up to US$10 million of its ordinary shares, approved by its Board. Repurchases may occur in open market, privately negotiated, or block trades under Rule 10b-18/10b5-1. Concurrently, controlling shareholder AMTD Digital Inc., directors, and management voluntarily agreed to a two-year lock-up on their TGE shares. TGE cites a 17.7% increase in total asset value to ~$1.7B and a 15.8% rise in net assets to ~$971M, viewing shares as undervalued. The repurchase aims to enhance shareholder value. Watch for execution pace and market conditions.

GIKLY.brief: Grifols SA filed a Form 6-K reporting results of its Ordinary General Shareholders' Meeting held June 18, 2026. Shareholders approved all agenda items except item eleventh regarding authorization to call extraordinary meetings with 15 days' notice. The meeting approved a mandatory preferred dividend of EUR 0.01 per Class B share and an ordinary dividend of EUR 56,065,663 from fiscal year 2025 profits, both payable July 2, 2026. The Board re-elected two directors: Montserrat Muñoz Abellana and Susana González Rodríguez. This is a routine corporate governance update with no special situation transaction disclosed.

IMCC.brief: IM Cannabis Corp. filed a 6-K announcing a non-binding letter of intent to sell its European activities via subsidiary IMC Holdings to Slil.com Holding Ltd., a related party controlled by CEO Oren Shuster. The consideration is the assumption of approximately CAD$10.5M in debt (CAD$7.5M retained liabilities plus CAD$3M short-term liabilities). No per-share price, premium, or implied value is stated. A special committee of independent directors was formed, and Beta Finance T.Y.S Ltd. was retained to assess fairness. The deal requires a definitive agreement, regulatory clearances, and is subject to an exclusivity period. This is a related-party divestiture aimed at deleveraging and focusing on Israeli operations; watch for shareholder opposition and regulatory scrutiny given the related-party nature.

INGVF.brief: ING Groep N.V. filed a Form 6-K attaching a press release announcing the appointment of Bob Bakker as head of Investor Relations, effective June 18, 2026. Bakker succeeds Sjoerd Miltenburg, who was appointed head of Wholesale Banking in the Netherlands. Bakker has been part of ING's IR team since 2019, most recently as Senior IR Officer, and will report to CFO Ida Lerner. No financial terms, shareholder vote, or regulatory approvals are required. This is a routine management change with no deal mechanics or risk-arb angle. What to watch: Bakker's communication strategy and any shifts in shareholder engagement.

ICCM.brief: IceCure Medical Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting a private placement of pre-funded warrants and Series D/E warrants with an institutional investor. The combined purchase price is $2.9999 per pre-funded warrant and accompanying warrants, implying gross proceeds of approximately $5.5 million. Pre-funded warrants are exercisable at $0.0001; Series D/E warrants at $3.00, expiring in five years and one year respectively. The company also amended existing Series B/C warrants to reduce exercise price from $16.50 to $3.00, subject to shareholder approval. A.G.P. acted as placement agent. The issuance increases potential share overhang upon exercise; watch for dilution effects and registration statement effectiveness timeline.

KB.brief: KB Financial Group Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting that its wholly-owned subsidiary Kookmin Bank declared an interim cash dividend of KRW 3,460 per common share, totaling approximately KRW 1.4 trillion. The record date is July 2, 2026, with payment expected on July 22, 2026. The entire dividend goes to the parent, KB Financial Group. This is a routine capital return event; the board resolved under Korean Commercial Code Article 53. No tender, acquisition, or restructuring. What to watch: whether KB Financial Group passes dividends to its own shareholders.

LGHL.brief: Lion Group Holding Ltd filed a Form 6-K announcing a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding to acquire 100% of Aquila Hash, Inc. The MOU provides for a 60-day mutual due diligence and exclusivity period, with final terms including structure and consideration to be defined in a definitive agreement. The transaction may be structured as a stock-for-stock acquisition. The MOU is non-binding except for customary provisions; no definitive agreement has been reached. The registrant acts as acquirer. No board recommendation, advisor, or specific deal terms are disclosed. Key watch items include due diligence outcomes and the risk that negotiations fail to produce a binding agreement.

LUD.brief: Luda Technology Group Ltd filed a Form 6-K announcing the resignation of Ms. Liu Liangping as a Director of the Board, effective June 18, 2026. Ms. Liu resigned to focus on the Company's merger and acquisition projects, and her resignation is not due to any disagreement with the Company or Board. She will remain as Chief Operating Officer and hold other subsidiary positions. No specific deal terms are disclosed. This is a routine management change with no special-situation financial transaction. Standard insider transition note; no risk-arb angle.

MEGL.brief: Magic Empire Global Limited filed a Form 6-K reporting the resignation of CFO Yau Ting Tai on June 15, 2026, for personal reasons, effective immediately, with no disagreement noted. On June 17, 2026, the Board appointed Mei Wang, age 54, a 33-year banking veteran from Agricultural Bank of China (most recently President of Jinan Free Trade Zone Sub-branch), as CFO. No material terms, consideration, or advisor were mentioned. This is a routine executive leadership change with no structural or economic impact on shareholders. The filing is a standard foreign private issuer report for a management change and does not involve a special situation.

OMH.brief: Ohmyhome Ltd filed a Form 6-K disclosing the sale of its wholly-owned subsidiary Ohmyhome (BVI) Ltd to Sterling Oat Ltd for $1. The board approved the divestiture after the target had negative net assets of $14.77M. The transaction closed on May 31, 2026. The price was nominal due to the subsidiary's weak financials; no premium applicable. The company exits real estate brokerage services to focus on digital marketing. No advisors named. Divestiture mechanics involve a share purchase agreement. The debt waiver of SGD 19M preceded the sale. Watch for the company's future performance in its new digital marketing focus.

PSORF.brief: Pearson plc filed a Form 6-K disclosing that its CEO, Omar Abbosh, has been appointed as a Non-Executive Director to the Board of Autodesk, Inc., effective June 17, 2026. The filing is made under UKLR 6.4.9R, a UK listing rule, which is the equivalent of a US disclosure of a director appointment under Form 8-K Item 5.02. No financial terms, share prices, or premiums are involved; no board recommendation or advisor is named. This is a routine governance change. The announcement signals no impact on Pearson's operations or strategy. What to watch: potential conflicts of interest or enhanced governance at Autodesk.

PRFX.brief: PRF Technologies Ltd. (Israel) filed a Form 6-K disclosing a Standby Equity Purchase Agreement with YA II PN, LTD. (Yorkville) on June 18, 2026. The company can sell up to $15.0 million of ordinary shares to Yorkville at 97% of the lowest three-day VWAP over 36 months. A 1.0% commitment fee is paid partly in 20,276 shares and cash installments. Yorkville's beneficial ownership is capped at 9.99%. Conditions include an SEC-registered resale statement. The prior May 2026 agreement for $10M terminated after full drawdown. This equity line provides flexible capital but is not a direct acquisition or going-private. Watch for dilutive issuance and stock price pressure.

RGNT.brief: Regentis Biomaterials Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting a registered direct offering of ordinary shares and warrants. On June 17, 2026, the company entered into securities purchase agreements with accredited and institutional investors to sell 1,844,543 ordinary shares and pre-funded warrants for 12,600 shares, plus ordinary warrants for 1,857,143 shares, at $3.50 per unit (or $3.4999 for pre-funded units). Gross proceeds are ~$6.5 million, with expected close on June 23, 2026. The pre-funded warrants have a $0.0001 exercise price; the ordinary warrants have a $4.20 exercise price, five-year term, and a 4.99% beneficial ownership blocker (up to 9.99% on notice). The company agreed to register resale shares within 15 trading days post-closing, with liquidated damages for delays. Net proceeds will fund clinical trials, regulatory submissions, manufacturing scale-up, European market entry, and working capital.

RLXXF.brief: This Form 6-K reports a director/PDMR shareholding transaction by RELX PLC, a foreign private issuer. On June 17, 2026, a PDMR was granted options over 922 ordinary shares under the RELX PLC ShareSave Plan 2023 at an exercise price of 19.728, with nil cost to the recipient. The filing is a routine disclosure of equity incentive grants to insiders under Rule 13a-16. No tender offer, acquisition, divestiture, activist campaign, strategic review, or capital return is involved. The report is neutral and administrative in nature, reflecting standard insider compensation disclosure requirements under UK regulations, mapped to US Form 8-K Item 5.02. What to watch: typical for insider grants with no market-moving implications.

AIIOW.brief: Robo.ai Inc. filed a Form 6-K reporting its indirect wholly owned subsidiary Roboai Investments L.L.C-FZ entering a Share Purchase Agreement dated June 12, 2026 to acquire 100% of QC Capital Limited, a BVI technology company, for 20,491,805 Class B ordinary shares valued at US$60,000,000. Sellers receive 3% at closing; remaining shares are locked up for 8 years, released in five equal annual tranches starting at the fourth anniversary. Closing is expected on or before July 24, 2026. The acquisition supports Robo.ai's technology development and global commercialization. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or break fee are stated. Watch for regulatory approvals and post-closing integration execution.

SGBAF.brief: SES filed a Form 6-K reporting the results of an Extraordinary General Meeting held on June 17, 2026. Shareholders approved the cancellation of shares repurchased under the company's buyback program initiated November 2, 2023 and amended May 2, 2024, resulting in a reduction of share capital. They also approved amendments to the company's articles of association regarding indemnification for board members and executives, and updates to shareholder meeting conduct. No specific terms such as price per share, premium, or deal value were disclosed. The filing does not reflect a typical special situation; it is a routine corporate governance update.

STN.brief: Stantec Inc. filed a Form 6-K and Material Change Report announcing the retirement of CEO Gordon A. Johnston effective October 1, 2026, and the appointment of Susan Reisbord as his successor. Mr. Johnston will remain as Vice Chair of the Board. Ms. Reisbord, previously COO for North America, joined Stantec in 2021 through the Cardno acquisition. The transition follows a Board-led succession plan. No financial terms, premiums, or shareholder votes are involved. The change is effective October 1, 2026. Watch for any strategic shifts under new leadership; no risk-arb angle as this is a routine executive succession.

TCMFF.brief: Telecom Argentina S.A. filed a Form 6-K reporting that the Argentine Antitrust Tribunal conditionally approved its acquisition of exclusive control over Telefónica Móviles Argentina S.A. and its subsidiaries. The approval requires divestiture remedies: transfer of at least 6,000,000 mobile customers (4,000,000 in AMBA, 2,000,000 elsewhere) plus related spectrum, and 211,400 residential internet subscribers in 28 localities across five provinces. Behavioral remedies apply in corporate and wholesale segments. The filing is a material event update following the earlier April 30, 2026 notice. No financial terms (price per share, premium, implied value) are disclosed. No board recommendation or named advisors. The regulatory conditionality and required asset divestitures represent key close-risk factors; watch for appointment of a divestiture trustee and progress on customer/spectrum transfers.

TIMB.brief: TIM S.A. filed a 6-K reporting its Fiscal Council's favorable opinion on a proposed distribution of Interest on Shareholders' Equity (IE) totaling R$400 million. The gross value per share is R$0.1674573219, with payment scheduled by July 22, 2026, to shareholders of record as of June 22, 2026 (ex-date June 23, 2026). A 17.5% withholding tax applies unless exempt. The gross per-share amount may adjust for treasury share variations. No board recommendation or advisor named. This is a capital return via IE, analogous to a dividend, not a special situation such as a tender offer or going-private. What to watch: actual payment date and any tax implications for foreign shareholders.

TII.brief: Titan Mining Corporation filed a Form 6-K on June 18, 2026, announcing the appointment of Richard Pozzebon as Chief Financial Officer, effective July 6, 2026. Mr. Pozzebon brings over 23 years of finance and capital markets experience, most recently as EVP and CFO of Interfor Corporation. He succeeds Interim CFO Ashley Kates, who will assist during the transition. The appointment supports Titan's strategic growth and project development in zinc concentrate and natural flake graphite. No deal terms are disclosed. The filing highlights a routine management change with no special situation implications.

UGP.brief: Ultrapar Holdings Inc. (via its Brazilian subsidiary Ultrapar Participações S.A.) filed a Form 6-K reporting board approval of a share buyback program. The company may repurchase up to 18,000,000 common shares (1.61% of capital stock) on B3 S.A. over 12 months ending June 17, 2027. The buyback is for stock-based incentive plans, treasury holding, or subsequent cancellation—no stated price or premium. No advisor or recommendation mentioned. The program complies with CVM Resolution 77/22. What to watch: pace of repurchases and potential for cancellation as a value-return signal; no risk-arb angle given open-market execution.

UMC.brief: United Microelectronics Corp filed a 6-K reporting the disposal of 2,896,036 common shares of Novatek Microelectronics Corporation at an average price of NTD 479.8 per share, for a total of NTD 1,389,518,072 (approximately USD 43M). The transaction occurred June 17-18, 2026, and is described as a shares conversion of zero-coupon exchangeable bonds due 2026. No board resolution or counterparty relationship was disclosed. The disposal resulted in a NTD 1,007,168,830 impact on retained earnings (no net income impact). After the trade, UMC holds 12,373,857 shares (2.03%) of Novatek. This is a routine bond conversion and securities sale, not a transformative special situation.

UXIN.brief: Uxin Ltd filed a Form 6-K on June 18, 2026, disclosing that Chairman and CEO Kun Dai intends to purchase up to US$5 million of the company's ADSs in the open market over a 12-month period starting June 25, 2026. The purchase reflects Dai's confidence in Uxin's value and long-term prospects amid headwinds in China's used car market. No specific price per share or premium was stated; the plan is voluntary and subject to insider trading policies. Uxin operates as a leading used car retailer in China. The buying plan signals insider alignment but does not alter corporate control. Watch for actual purchases and any subsequent ownership increases.

VODPF.brief: Vodafone Group Plc filed a Form 6-K with the SEC, incorporating legal opinions from Linklaters LLP (Exhibits 5.1 and 5.2) related to the issuance of U.S.$1,000,000,000 4.800% Notes due 2031, U.S.$1,000,000,000 5.350% Notes due 2036, and U.S.$1,500,000,000 6.100% Notes due 2056. This is a routine debt offering with no special situation elements such as acquisitions, divestitures, or activist campaigns. The filing does not include transaction terms, premiums, or board recommendations; it purely covers the legal validity of the notes under English law.

ATXG.brief: Addentax Group Corp. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of a share exchange on June 15, 2026. Through its Hong Kong subsidiary, it acquired a 41.67% stake in Riches Family Office Limited (Target) from Riches FO Holdings Limited and its sole shareholder, Mr. Wu Rui, the company’s COO. Consideration was 33,500 shares of Addentax common stock, issued under Regulation S (offshore, no U.S. person). No cash, premium, or board advisor named. The stake creates cross-ownership with management. Watch for minority-interest governance, potential consolidation, and any future buyout of the remaining stake.

ATNM.brief: Actinium Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K disclosing its compliance plan submitted to NYSE American to address non-compliance with continued listing standards (Section 1003(a)(ii): stockholders' equity below $4.0 million with losses in three of four recent years). The plan outlines actions management intends to take to regain compliance. No specific financial or operational terms were provided. The company previously received a deficiency notice on May 27, 2026. The NYSE American will review the plan and grant a cure period. Watch for exchange decision on plan acceptance and potential delisting if compliance is not restored.

RIME.brief: Algorhythm Holdings, Inc. disclosed it received a Nasdaq deficiency notice on June 16, 2026, for failing the $1.00 minimum bid price rule under Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) based on 30 consecutive business days. The company has a 180-day cure period through December 14, 2026. Compliance can be regained if the closing bid price is at least $1.00 for ten consecutive business days; Nasdaq may require a longer period. A second 180-day period may be available if other listing standards are met. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The stock (RIME) continues trading. Key risk: potential delisting if bid price fails to recover; a reverse stock split may be considered.

BCBP.brief: BCB Bancorp, Inc. filed an 8-K on June 18, 2026, announcing that its Board of Directors voted to suspend quarterly cash dividends on common and preferred stock, and also suspend its 2026 Amended and Restated Dividend Reinvestment and Stock Purchase Plan. The suspension is effective immediately, as disclosed in an attached press release. No exact terms such as dividend amount or premium were stated. The filing does not mention any board recommendation, advisor, acquisition, or structural mechanics. This action likely reflects capital preservation amid economic uncertainties. No deal terms exist; there is no risk-arb angle, as this is a payout policy change, not a transaction.

BFNH.brief: BioForce Nanosciences Holdings filed an 8-K reporting a change of control on April 15, 2026. Director Merle Ferguson sold 26.7 million common shares (79.65% of outstanding stock) to Nexus Capital Investments for $400,000 in corporate funds, with no loans involved. This private transaction resulted in a change of control. Subsequently, on June 17, 2026, Co-CEOs Steven Gagnon and John LaViolette, and VP Sasha Shapiro resigned, and Scott Mager was appointed director. No board recommendation or advisor named. The filing is classified as 'Other' as the transaction is a privately negotiated stock sale and concurrent management change, not a public acquisition or tender offer.

BRC.brief: Brady Corp filed an 8-K regarding entry into a $1.0 billion Credit Agreement to finance its pending acquisition of Honeywell International's Productivity Solutions and Services (PSS) business. The facility comprises a $500 million term loan and a $500 million revolving credit facility, maturing June 12, 2031. Brady replaced and terminated its prior credit agreement, exchanging $13 million in revolving loans. The revolver is capped at $300 million pre-closing and expands to $500 million post-closing. Joint lead arrangers include BMO Capital Markets, BofA Securities, CIBC, PNC, and Wells Fargo. Collateral and leverage-based pricing apply. Watch for PSS deal closing and integration risk.

BCO.brief: The Brink's Company filed an 8-K disclosing an acquisition of NCR Atleos Corporation via a two-step merger. On February 26, 2026, Brink's, NCR Atleos, and merger subsidiaries entered into a merger agreement where Merger Sub I will merge into NCR Atleos, followed by a second merger into Merger Sub II. The S-4 registration statement was declared effective on May 27, 2026. Special meetings are set for June 30, 2026, for shareholder votes. Two shareholder lawsuits filed in New York Supreme Court challenge the merger, alleging negligent misrepresentation in NCR Atleos's proxy statement. Watch for litigation outcomes and shareholder approval; the risk-arb spread may reflect deal uncertainty.

DYAI.brief: Dyadic International received a Nasdaq delisting notice on June 18, 2026 for failing to comply with Bid Price Rule 5450(a)(1) (minimum $1.00 bid) and Continued Listing Standard 5550(b) (equity/market cap/income). The company was previously given 180 days to cure the bid price deficiency, expiring June 17, 2026, and was eligible for an additional 180 days only if it met $5M shareholders' equity—which it did not. Dyadic will request a hearing, which automatically stays delisting until a panel decision. If uncured, the company may face transfer to OTC markets; risk-arb angle: delisting risk limits liquidity and financing options.

ALISU.brief: Calisa Acquisition Corp, a SPAC, filed an S-4 registration statement for its proposed business combination with Goodvision AI Inc. The transaction will see Calisa acquire Goodvision AI, with Goodvision's shareholders receiving Calisa ordinary shares. The deal implies an enterprise value of approximately $300 million. The board of Calisa recommends the transaction, which is expected to close in Q4 2026. The merger requires shareholder approval and regulatory reviews. Key mechanics include redemption rights for Calisa's public shareholders and a potential overhang from the SPAC's trust. Risk-arbitrage focus: monitor shareholder redemption levels and regulatory clearance timeline.

DAAQU.brief: Digital Asset Acquisition Corp. (DAAC) filed an amended S-4/A for its business combination with Old Glory Holding Co. The filing updates the registration statement covering the issuance of DAAC shares to Old Glory shareholders. No specific per-share price, premium, or expected closing date is provided in the excerpt. The board's recommendation and advisor names are not disclosed. Structurally, DAAC is a blank-check company; the combined entity will inherit the trust proceeds. Key items include managing potential shareholder redemptions. Watch for the final proxy mailing and shareholder vote. The risk-arb angle focuses on the spread versus the trust value and any redemption pressure.

MCFN.brief: McCarthy Finney, Inc. filed Amendment No. 1 to Form S-4 (SEC file 333-295888) on June 18, 2026, relating to an unspecified business combination. The filing includes financial statements and pro forma data for Q1 2026, referencing series B and C preferred stock, common stock, stock options, RSUs, and equity line agreements. No specific terms (price, premium, close date) are stated. The board's recommendation and advisor are not disclosed. The S-4/A is a registration statement for securities to be issued in a merger or acquisition. Watch for the definitive S-4 with detailed deal terms and the target's identity to assess risk-arb spread.

PRIF-PL.brief: Priority Income Fund, Inc. commenced an issuer tender offer to repurchase up to 1,550,812 shares (2.5% of outstanding) at a cash price equal to net asset value per share as of July 31, 2026. The April 30, 2026 NAV was $3.70/share, but the purchase price may differ. The offer aims to provide liquidity as there is no public market. The board has not disclosed a recommendation or advisor. The offer expires on a date not yet specified in the excerpt. Mechanics are subject to conditions. The deal is a self-tender at NAV; watch for the final NAV calculation and proration given the small percentage sought.

IOBTQ.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist IO Biotech, Inc.'s common stock effective June 18, 2026. The delisting follows Nasdaq Staff's determination on March 31, 2026, that the company no longer met listing requirements under Rules 5101, 5110(b), and IM-5101-1. IO Biotech did not appeal the determination; its stock was suspended on April 7, 2026, when the delisting became final. No board recommendation, advisor, or deal terms were disclosed. The delisting removes exchange trading; shares may trade OTC. Watch for potential OTC market liquidity and any subsequent corporate actions.

CXE.brief: NYSE filed Form 25-NSE to delist MFS High Income Municipal Trust (CMU) after its merger with Aberdeen Municipal Income Fund closed June 8, 2026. Each CMU share converted into 0.68270092 Aberdeen shares. The board recommended the merger; no advisor named. Mechanics: stock consideration, all-share exchange with no cash component. Overhang eliminated; 0% premium implied by fixed ratio. Regulatory clock: delisting effective June 22. What to watch: risk-arb spread narrows as conversion ratio is fixed; focus on Aberdeen Fund's post-merger NAV performance.

ATYR.brief: aTyr Pharma disclosed via 8-K that on June 3, 2026, Nasdaq granted the company an additional 180-day compliance period, through November 30, 2026, to cure its bid price deficiency (shares closed below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days). The initial compliance period expired June 2, 2026. The Staff determined the company meets all other continued listing standards. aTyr must show a closing bid of at least $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days. The company may effect a reverse stock split if needed. No board recommendation or advisor was named. Risk-arb angle: monitor near-term bid price action and any reverse-split announcement; failure by Nov. 30 could trigger delisting proceedings.

APURU.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist Aperture AC (CIK 0002093524), a blank-check company, under Section 12d2-2(a)(2) of the 1934 Act. The delisting is effective June 9, 2026. No terms, premium, or board recommendation are disclosed. The filing removes the security from exchange listing; no collateral, overhang, or ownership split is involved. Regulatory clock is immediate. What to watch: risk-arb focus is on whether Aperture AC has completed or abandoned a de-SPAC business combination; delisting may precede liquidation or a going-private transaction.

BREZU.brief: Nasdaq filed Form 25-NSE to strike Breeze Acquisition Corp. II from listing under 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(a)(2), effective June 10, 2026. The delisting follows the SPAC's failure to maintain compliance; no merger or shareholder vote is involved. The removal is administrative, with no deal terms, premium, or advisor referenced. Shares became worthless upon delisting; the filing confirms cessation of trading. What to watch: potential liquidation trust distribution (if any) or litigation over the blank-check company's dissolution; no risk-arb angle as the vehicle is defunct.

JSPRW.brief: On June 3, 2026, Jasper Therapeutics disclosed receiving a Nasdaq notice for non-compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price rule (Listing Rule 5550(a)(2)) on the Nasdaq Capital Market. The company has 180 calendar days, until November 30, 2026, to regain compliance by having its voting common stock close at $1.00 or more for at least ten consecutive business days. There is no immediate impact on listing or trading of shares (JSPR) or warrants (JSPRW). If non-compliance persists, Jasper may qualify for a second 180-day cure period, subject to meeting other initial listing standards and potentially implementing a reverse stock split. The company is evaluating available options to address the deficiency.

IPDN.brief: Professional Diversity Network, Inc. disclosed in an 8-K filed June 9, 2026, that on June 5, 2026, it received a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to meet the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement (Rule 5550(a)(2)), as its closing bid price remained below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days. The company received a 180-day compliance period through December 2, 2026, to regain compliance by closing at or above $1.00 for ten consecutive business days. If unsuccessful, it may qualify for a second 180-day period. Shares continue trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market during this time. The company is evaluating measures to address the deficiency but provides no assurance of regaining compliance or avoiding delisting. Risk-arb angle: monitor for reverse stock split or other curative actions; failure could lead to OTC trading and further dilution.

AVGO.brief: Broadcom Inc. filed an S-4 registration statement with the SEC on June 9, 2026, relating to an exchange offer. The company is offering to exchange up to $3,249,984,000 of its 3.137% Senior Notes due 2035 and up to $2,750,000,000 of its 3.187% Senior Notes due 2036, issued September 30, 2021, for registered notes with substantially identical terms. The exchange is intended to satisfy registration obligations. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or timeline is specified. The transaction is a registered exchange, not a new issuance, with no cash consideration. Risk-arb angle: minimal, as exchange offers typically carry low execution risk; watch for SEC effectiveness and any proration or oversubscription details.

SOBR.brief: SOBR Safe, Inc. filed an S-4 registration statement on June 9, 2026, relating to a business combination or similar transaction. The filing discloses insider trading policies but does not provide deal terms, premium, or specific transaction structure. No board recommendation or advisors are named in the excerpt. The filing appears to be a preliminary registration, and the SEC review process will determine effectiveness. Investors should watch for a definitive proxy statement/prospectus detailing the merger consideration, shareholder vote, and closing mechanics. The risk-arb spread and regulatory timeline are unclear pending further disclosures.

GPUS-PD.brief: Hyperscale Data, Inc. filed Amendment No. 3 to its Schedule TO, announcing final results of its issuer tender offer that expired June 8, 2026. The tender offer, launched May 26, 2026, was for shares of its Class A Common Stock. The board of directors recommended the offer. The press release detailing final results is incorporated by reference. This amendment satisfies Rule 13e-4(c)(4) reporting requirements. No financial terms were disclosed in this filing. Watch for the final accepted share count and proration factor.

LEGT-UN.brief: NYSE American LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist Legato Merger Corp. III after its business combination with Einride AB became effective on June 9, 2026. Under the terms, each Legato ordinary share was cancelled and exchanged for one Einride ADS; each warrant was converted into one Einride warrant; units separated into components. No price per share, implied value, or premium was disclosed. The delisting is effective June 22, 2026. All securities were suspended from trading on June 10, 2026. This is a de-SPAC closing, with no further structural notes or regulatory clock beyond the delisting. Watch for post-combination trading of Einride ADS and any potential redemption or overhang from unexchanged shares.

MLACR.brief: The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist Mountain Lake Acquisition Corp. (CIK 0002029492) pursuant to Rule 12d2-2(a)(3). The delisting applies to the company's Class A ordinary shares, rights, and units. No purchase price or premium is involved. The board recommendation and advisor are not stated. This is a regulatory delisting action by the exchange effective June 11, 2026, based on the issuer's non-compliance. No risk-arb angle is present; the filing indicates the securities will no longer trade on Nasdaq. What to watch: any subsequent delisting under Rule 12d2-2(b) if the company seeks to go private.

TPTA.brief: Terra Property Trust filed Amendment No. 3 to its S-4 registration statement on June 11, 2026, in connection with an exchange offer. The company extended the expiration date from June 25 to June 26, 2026, and amended terms of the exchange offer and exchange notes. A non-binding indication of interest from holders representing ~65.7% of existing notes principal was received, but no assurance of tender. Terra will pay up to $300,000 of participating holders' out-of-pocket fees. The exchange offer is registered under the Securities Act; effectiveness of the registration statement is required before securities can be issued. Watch for definitive participation levels and regulatory clearance.

FITBP.brief: Fifth Third Bancorp voluntarily filed Form 25 to delist and deregister its common stock and four series of preferred depositary shares from the Nasdaq Stock Market. The board authorized the withdrawal under Exchange Act Rule 12d2-2(c), effective immediately upon filing. No stake, price or premium was disclosed, as the action is not a merger. The delisting may precede a going-private transaction or regulatory restructuring; watch for subsequent filings detailing a tender offer, shareholder vote or Schedule 13E-3. Risk-arb attention centers on liquidity loss and potential buyout terms.

YHNAU.brief: YHN Acquisition I Ltd disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq deficiency notice on June 10, 2026, for failing the minimum 400 total holders requirement under Listing Rule 5450(a)(2). The SPAC has 45 days to submit a compliance plan; Nasdaq may grant up to 180 days to cure. The company may also apply to transfer to the Nasdaq Capital Market ($5,000 fee). No board recommendation or advisor named. Units, ordinary shares, and rights continue trading under YHNAU, YHNA, YHNAR. Watch: whether a business combination or holder outreach is used to regain compliance, and potential delisting risk if plan is rejected.

BKHAU.brief: Black Hawk Acquisition Corp, a SPAC, filed an amended S-4 for its business combination with Vesicor Therapeutics. The SPAC will domesticate from Cayman Islands to Delaware before closing. Terms (stake, price, premium) are not disclosed in this filing. The board recommends the deal; legal advisors include Celine Partners, Winston Taylor LLP, and PW Richter PLC. Mechanics: Vesicor shareholders will receive SPAC stock. The transaction is subject to SEC effectiveness and shareholder approval. Watch for regulatory clearance timeline and potential shareholder redemptions.

BCARU.company: D. Boral ARC Acquisition I Corp.
BCARU.brief: D. Boral ARC Acquisition I Corp. (a SPAC) filed an amended S-4/A for its merger with Exascale Labs Inc., a prepackaged software firm. The filing does not disclose specific per-share price, premium, or implied valuation. Under the business combination, D. Boral ARC will acquire Exascale Labs; the target's shareholders will receive shares in the combined entity. The board of D. Boral ARC recommends the deal. Mechanically, the merger will be effected through a merger subsidiary; existing SPAC shareholders may redeem their shares. Regulatory clock is governed by SEC review of the S-4. Watch for shareholder redemption levels and FTC/HSR clearance timeline as risk-arb catalysts.

SWDR.company: Starwood Real Estate Income Trust, Inc.

FACWW.brief: On June 5, 2026, the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed a Form 25-NSE with the SEC to delist Factorial Energy Inc. (formerly Cartesian Growth Corp III), effective immediately. The delisting is under 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(a)(3), typically for failure to meet listing standards. Factorial Energy, a DE-incorporated electrical machinery manufacturer, was listed under SEC file number 333-284565. No board recommendation, advisor, or shareholder vote was required. The delisting is effective as of the filing date, removing the security from Nasdaq. What to watch: whether the company will appeal or seek OTCQX/OTCQB listing; risk-arb perspective is moot as there is no acquisition premium.

ARAI.brief: Arrive AI Inc. disclosed on Form 8-K that it received a Nasdaq deficiency notice on June 2, 2026, for failing to maintain the $1.00 minimum bid price for 30 consecutive business days (Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1)). The company has a 180-day compliance period, until November 30, 2026, to regain compliance. If not met, it may qualify for a second 180-day period if it meets other initial listing standards. There is no board recommendation, advisor, or deal mechanics. The stock remains listed; risk-arb watchers should monitor price action and any potential reverse stock split or other remedy.
